en: The Śrīśivarakṣāstotra (The Auspicious Hymn for Protection by Śiva)
Oṃ. Of this great mantra, the Śrī Śivarakṣāstotra, Yājñavalkya is the seer (ṛṣi),
the venerable Sadāśiva is the deity (devatā),
and Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ).
The application (viniyoga) is for the recitation of the Śrī Śivarakṣā Stotra for the sake of pleasing the venerable Sadāśiva.
The purifying life-story of Mahādeva, the God of gods,
which is boundless, supremely noble, and the means for attaining the four aims of human existence;
[the story] of the five-faced, three-eyed Lord accompanied by Gaurī and Vināyaka.
Having meditated upon the ten-armed Śiva, a person should recite the *Śivarakṣā*:

"May the bearer of the Gaṅgā protect my head; may he whose crest is the crescent moon protect my forehead. May the destroyer of Madana protect my eyes; may he adorned with serpents protect my ears. (2–3)
May the Enemy of Tripura protect my nose; may the Lord of the World protect my face;
may the Lord of Speech protect my tongue; and may the Moon-crested One protect my neck.
May Śrīkaṇṭha protect my throat, and may the Bearer of the Universe’s Burden protect my shoulders.
May the wielder of the Pināka bow protect my two arms; may he who removes the burden of the earth protect my hands.
May Śaṅkara protect my heart, and the Lord of the Daughter of the Mountain protect my belly.
May the Conqueror of Death protect my navel, and he whose garment is a tiger skin protect my hips.
May He who is compassionate toward the distressed protect my two thighs;
may Maheśvara protect my two upper legs; may Jagadīśvara protect my knees.
May the Creator of the World protect my shanks; may Gaṇādhipa protect my ankles.
The Ocean of Compassion [bestows] the two feet, and Sadāśiva [bestows] all the limbs.
That virtuous person who recites this protection, endowed with the power of Śiva,
shall enjoy all desires and attain union with Śiva.
Those who roam the three worlds, such as planets, spirits, and piśācas,
flee swiftly from afar due to the protection afforded by the name of Śiva.
This armor of the Lord of Pārvatī is named "The Bestower of Fearlessness."
For him who wears this on his neck with devotion, the three worlds are under his control.
(11) Just as Nārāyaṇa instructed this protection of Śiva in a dream, so did Yājñavalkya, the lord of yogis, write it down upon waking in the morning. (12)
Thus ends the Śrīśivarakṣāstotra proclaimed by the venerable Yājñavalkya.
